subject.title: feat(onboarding): offer detected Claude Code/Codex/Hermes memory imports across CLI, macOS, and Linux onboarding

question: Should local onboarding permanently add a detection-gated memory-import page across CLI, macOS, and Linux/Control UI once the apply operation cannot block setup indefinitely?
rationale: The implementation changes a prominent first-run journey on four surfaces; code review can require safe execution, but it cannot decide whether this additional onboarding choice is the intended long-term product experience.

options.title: Approve after bounded apply
options.body: Keep the cross-surface feature, but require timeout/cancellation recovery and completed live first-run proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the rollout
options.body: Keep memory-only Hermes support and the existing Settings import page while limiting or postponing additional onboarding prompts.

options.title: Defer onboarding integration
options.body: Pause the PR until the migration backup hang is fixed and the desired first-run UX is reconsidered.

recommendation.title: Approve after bounded apply
recommendation.body: Keep the cross-surface feature, but require timeout/cancellation recovery and completed live first-run proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history spans the primary setup flow, Hermes migration, and adjacent onboarding architecture, making them the strongest available product-routing candidate.
